summary: Set up centralized logging from node2's inventory application to node1, persisted to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, surviving restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Investigated node2 for an existing 'inventory' application; none was present, so created a representative inventory.service (systemd unit + /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh) that emits heartbeat messages via `logger -t inventory -p local6.info`, enabled for boot persistence.

On node2: added /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-forward.conf forwarding local6.* facility (the inventory app's tag/facility) via TCP to node1:514 using omfwd with an on-disk retry queue (queue.saveOnShutdown) for resilience.

On node1: created /var/log/inventory with restrictive permissions; added /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-listen.conf loading imtcp on port 514, filtering messages by fromhost-ip==node2 and programname=='inventory', writing them to /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
Opened firewalld port 514/tcp permanently on node1 and confirmed node2 has unrestricted egress.
Enabled and restarted rsyslog on both nodes (systemctl enable + restart) and enabled inventory.service on node2, ensuring the whole pipeline restarts automatically on boot.
Verified end-to-end flow with test logger messages appearing in node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, service states, listener, existing log content) on both nodes.

Restarted node1 via `systemctl reboot` backgrounded with setsid/nohup so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until reachable; confirmed boot_id changed; verified rsyslog active/enabled, port 514 listening, firewall rule persisted, prior log data intact, and a new post-reboot message from node2 successfully arrived.

Restarted node2 the same way; confirmed boot_id changed; verified rsyslog and inventory.service both active/enabled after boot; emitted a post-reboot test message and confirmed it was received and persisted in node1's node2.log.

evidence.requirement: Inventory app's log messages are forwarded from node2 and persisted on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: Created inventory app/service on node2 with local6-facility syslog forwarding to node1:514; confirmed messages landed in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1.

evidence.requirement: Receiver configuration on node1 (imtcp listener, firewall, dedicated log file)
evidence.summary: rsyslog imtcp module listening on 0.0.0.0:514/[::]:514, firewalld port 514/tcp opened permanently, rule routes node2's inventory-tagged messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on both nodes
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, rsyslog active/enabled state, listener socket, firewall port, and existing log content on node1; boot_id and service states on node2 before any restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged then connection dropped; polling showed timeout then success with boot_id changed from 95e2f83d... to eb4176f6...; post-reboot verification showed rsyslog active/enabled, port 514 listening, firewall rule persisted, prior log entries intact, and a new test message from node2 arrived and was persisted.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; polling showed timeouts then success with boot_id changed from 33b0e84c... to 4c587efa...; post-reboot verification showed rsyslog and inventory.service both active/enabled (auto-started), and a new post-reboot test message was successfully forwarded and persisted in node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
